summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old male with a history of kidney transplantation, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, atrial fibrillation, and heart failure was admitted for persistent diarrhea and abdominal cramping following a recent hospitalization. He was diagnosed with recurrent C. difficile colitis, likely triggered by recent antibiotic use. He also presented with acute kidney injury secondary to dehydration and tacrolimus toxicity, with elevated creatinine and hyperkalemia. He was treated with intravenous fluids, oral vancomycin taper, and dose reduction of tacrolimus. His atrial fibrillation was managed with temporary metoprolol and warfarin dose adjustment due to an elevated INR. Renal function improved to baseline, diarrhea resolved, and he was discharged on a prolonged vancomycin taper, reduced tacrolimus, and stable anticoagulation, with plans for fecal transplant evaluation and close outpatient follow-up.
